result.reason: 2 findings, both important (missing tests), and 4 dropped.

findings.label: F6
findings.problem: openTimeInMinutesOf() has two new ways to return null that no test checks. It returns null when dateOf() is null, which happens while the itinerary has no start date. It also returns null when the stop's timeline entry has no startMinute or endMinute, such as when the leg isn't routed for the day's selected places. The only null tests cover a place with no opening periods (Fisher Towers) and a stop with no selected place.
findings.failure_case: Delete `|| date === null` from the check, and guard the weekday read some other way. Or delete the `entry.startMinute === null || entry.endMinute === null` check, so openMinutesWithin runs with null minutes and returns 0. Every test in calendar-schedule.test.ts still passes. A caller such as approveOpeningHours() would then record 0 open minutes for a stop whose times just aren't known yet.
findings.label_reason: These are new behaviors, visible to callers as a null result, that the change adds and no test would catch if removed, so F6 fits. Labels above it don't fit, because the code itself behaves correctly.

findings.label: F6
findings.problem: scheduleTimeAt() returns null for any minute of 2880 or more, so a time later than the next calendar day is left empty. No test reaches a schedule time that far out. The Moab Day 4 test ends at 2:15 a.m. the next day, which is well under 2880.
findings.failure_case: Delete `|| minute >= 2 * MINUTES_IN_DAY`. A minute of 3000 then becomes 2:00 a.m. with isNextDay true, which is a wrong time one day early. Every test still passes.
findings.label_reason: The cap is new behavior that a caller of scheduleOf() could see, and no test would fail without it, so F6 fits. The code is correct as written, so F1 to F5 don't fit.

dropped.problem: openMinutesWithin could count the same open minutes twice, because each period is checked at four week shifts (-1, 0, 1 and 2).
dropped.label: D1
dropped.reason: A period lasts at most one week. It is open to close, plus 10080 minutes when close <= open. The shifted copies are 10080 minutes apart, so they never overlap, and no minute of the visit can fall in two of them.

dropped.problem: The seasonal window check could be broken if CalendarDate.compareTo() returned only the sign (-1, 0 or 1), since `>= -7` would then always be true.
dropped.label: D1
dropped.reason: compareTo() in calendar-date.ts returns the rounded number of days between the two dates. The test at calendar-weather.test.ts line 140 checks the 7-day and 8-day boundaries.

dropped.problem: Stops with no selected place are pushed after the drive to the next selected stop, which could put the entries out of time order.
dropped.label: D1
dropped.reason: The next stop's arrival is max(earliest, heldUntil, setMinute), and heldUntil includes each waiting stop's time. So the drive ends at or after every waiting stop's time, and the order matches what the code comment says.

dropped.problem: The free-time entry could end before it starts, or get a negative drive start.
dropped.label: D1
dropped.reason: Free time is pushed only when arrival > earliest, and earliest = departure + drive. So arrival - drive is always greater than departure, and the drive's start is never earlier than departure.
